title: Metering Sidecar: Lease-Window Tokens for Deterministic Billing and Idempotent Ingest
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a lightweight metering sidecar that emits deterministic billing tokens (lease-window tokens) per logical ingestion to prevent duplicate charging under at-least-once delivery semantics. The sidecar sits alongside the ingestion frontends and implements a bounded dedupe window using token expiry, a per-customer monotonic sequence stamp for ledger commits, and optimistic commit attestations to avoid double consumption on retries/timeouts.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar generates deterministic billing token for every incoming logical request using client idempotency key + received-timestamp truncated to lease window + customer-sequence-id
Server-side ledger accepts token-anchored commits and rejects duplicate token commits within token TTL
Canary rollout to 1% of accounts shows <0.05% increase in 99th percentile latency and zero confirmed double-billing incidents over 72 hours
Migration path exists for clients without idempotency keys (server falls back to sequence-stamp only with stronger lease window)
design_decisions: Use a sidecar rather than global gateway to localize transient state and reduce cross-region coordination costs
Token design: H(customer_id || idempotency_key || window_start || sequence_hint) using HMAC with KMS-managed key to ensure non-forgeability
Lease-window length default: 90s (configurable per customer) to balance duplicate risk vs cache size
Persist only token -> commit reference (small footprint) in per-customer ledger with TTL; avoid storing full request payload in dedupe index
Optimistic commit attestation: backend returns commit_ticket (sequence number + signature) for sidecar to ack; sidecar retries idempotently using ticket
implementation_notes: Sidecar API: /emit-token (sync) and /confirm-commit (async). /emit-token returns token + expiry; clients include token in ingestion request headers.
Backend ledger changes: add 'token_index' table with key (customer_id, token) -> commit_ticket; uniqueness constraint ensures single successful commit per token
Concurrency: use lightweight conditional writes (DynamoDB conditional put or Postgres INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + select-after-insert) to guarantee single commit wins
Fallback: if client provides no idempotency key, sidecar will synthesize a pseudo-key from request fingerprint + timestamp but with shorter lease window and higher conservative billing flags
Interplay with rate limiter/quotas: sidecar consults local quota snapshot to surface early rejections and tags tokens with quota_version to enable audit and replay safety
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit + integration tests covering token collisions, TTL expiry, and optimistic commit failure modes
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 1% of customers behind feature flag; monitor dedupe_hit_rate and billing anomalies dashboard
Phase 2 (regional expand): enable across single region for 10% of traffic; enable additional logging and sampling of requests for forensic replay
Phase 3 (global): 100% enable with automated cleanup job to GC expired tokens and backfill commit attestations for long-running requests
Rollback: circuit-breaker to disable sidecar token acceptance and fall back to current global nonce scheme within 1 minute
